Proof-of-concept report · Quality screening

Can a phone photo flag stem adulteration in red chilli powder?

A lighting-robust image method counts elongated pale particles (stem-like fibres) per unit powder area. On a pure sample vs a 10% stem-spiked sample, the spiked one scored consistently higher. This page shows the method and the evidence.

278 → 378fibres per megapixel, control → 10% stem
1.31–1.40×stem/control ratio, stable across lighting and threshold changes
Same resultafter changing brightness and detection thresholds

How it works

Segment
Keep only the orange-red powder heap. White background, blue strip and stray dust are removed.
Compare locally
Each pixel is compared with its own neighbourhood, so a brighter or dimmer photo does not fake a result.
Filter by shape
Keep only particles 3× longer than wide (10–80 px). Stem fibres are thin and stick-like.
Normalise
Count ÷ powder area (MP) gives a density comparable across photos.
